evidence.note: First actions build baseline.py (reference PyTorch TriMul) and benchmark it before writing any kernel — a reference oracle as the first milestone.
Straightforward kernel + dedicated test.py, explicit TodoWrite milestone planning (15), correctness test against baseline, then benchmark — ordered stages each with a done-check.
Distinct correctness-debugging phase (check_fail.py, value ranges) with TodoWrite at 49, resolving correctness before committing to heavy optimization.

Optimization decomposed into per-component tuning harnesses (perm_test, ln_test, bmm_test, proj_test, mm_test, tail_test, lpg_test), each independently tuned — the optimization stage itself is broken into sub-milestones.
full_test.py full-grid correctness sweep plus edge-case tests late in the run; pervasive 'Test+bench' steps re-verify correctness after each optimization, guarding against fast-but-wrong regressions.

reasoning: The agent built a reference oracle first, matched a straightforward kernel to it with a dedicated test, resolved correctness across failure cases, then entered a decomposed optimization phase where each component had its own tuning harness and every optimization step was paired with a correctness re-check — matching anchor 8's ordered milestones with concrete exit tests and reaching into 10-territory via decomposed optimization with per-milestone checks. It stops short of a full 10 because performance and correctness interleave with continuous re-verification rather than performance being a strictly separate track gated on a frozen baseline, and explicit risk-sequencing of the hardest Cauchy/large-N cases first is not evident in the log.
